title: Self-dual random-cluster interfaces below one
coverage:
The paper is about 16k lines of LaTeX, so this was a partial audit. Read in full: Introduction, Section 1 (site pressure, adjacent/cofacial Rayleigh, network monotonicity, rooted coverage, no-hit comparison, interlacing gluing), the holomorphicity theorem, the boundary-problem identification and fixed-polygon formula (Sec 7, from line 2100 to the end), the first ~620 lines of Sec 8 (access lemma, inset cuts/seams, electrode-update cost, moving two-terminal crossing proof including cofacial peeling), and the six-vertex free-energy and vacuum-normalization part of Sec 6.

Checks I ran:
(a) Brute force on 3000 random small graphs with q in (0,1): adjacent edges never had positive covariance (max about 1e-15).
(b) Brute force: P_{H/S}(a<->S) <= P_H(a<->S), and the root correlation P(a<->o, b<->o) >= P(a<->o)P(b<->o), both with no violations.
(c) Hand-checked the sign bookkeeping in the -log F coefficient proof, using Dong/Jackson–Sokal negativity and the (-1)^{b-1} hard-edge sum.
(d) Quadrilateral: with y=e^{i lambda}, the side vectors, angles 0, pi-lambda, 2lambda, pi+lambda, exterior turns summing to 2pi, and interior angles lambda, lambda, 2pi-3lambda, lambda all check out. The Schwarz–Christoffel exponents rho-1, rho-1, 1-3rho, and the -1-rho decay at infinity, are correct.
(e) Numerically, r(chi)+r(1-chi)=1 for several rho and chi.
(f) The duality map H(p)=(1-p)/(1-(1-q)p) is correct; I derived it from rewiring A and B through the exterior. H(g(chi))=g(1-chi) also checks.
(g) The cap reweighting r/(r+d(1-r)) is correct.
(h) kappa=4pi/arccos(-sqrt q/2)=4/(1-rho) is correct.
(i) Six-vertex: Delta=(2a*^2-1)/(2a*^2)=-cos(lambda) is correct, and the monotone-trace and seam-gluing lower bound Lambda_N >= F(lambda/2)^{N/2} is sound.

Not verified line by line: Sections 2–5 (rectangle RSW, sectors, irregular-disk decay and routing, angular transfer), most of Sec 6 (charge budget), Sec 7 before line 2100 (factorization, gap closure, normalized diagonal cancellation, mixed-derivative saving), the driver identification and C2 tightness in Sec 8, and the appendices. Those analytic estimates carry most of the proof and remain unaudited.
main_claim: For every fixed 0<q<1, the Dobrushin (wired/free) interface of the square-lattice random-cluster model at p=sqrt q/(1+sqrt q) converges, in smooth Jordan domains approximated by simple lattice polygons, to chordal SLE_kappa with kappa=4pi/arccos(-sqrt q/2) in (6,8). Convergence is in the uniform metric on oriented curves modulo reparametrization, along the full mesh sequence.
sibling_notes: The board for family 223 (hive:oai_math:review:fam:223) was empty when I checked, so no sibling input was used. The paper's Corollary 1.3 relies on the companion paper OpenAI2026FKInterfacesAboveOne (Theorem 1.1(i)) for the range 1<=q<4. That reduction is a short marginalisation over the wired-arc edges, and it checks out. The main theorem for q<1 does not depend on the companion paper.
